title: Affine elementary etale finite-over-smooth local structure
statement: Let $p:Z\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $z\in Z$, put $s=p(z)$, and let $n=\dim_z(Z_s)$ for $Z_s=Z\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-residue-field, def-kun-dimension]. There exist affine schemes $W,Y,S_1$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], points $w\in W$, $y\in Y$, $s_1\in S_1$, and morphisms $b:W\to Z$, $a:S_1\to S$, $\pi:W\to Y$, $h:Y\to S_1$ with $pb=ah\pi$, $b(w)=z$, $\pi(w)=y$, and $h(y)=s_1$, such that $b$ and $a$ are etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] and induce isomorphisms $\kappa(z)\cong\kappa(w)$ and $\kappa(s)\cong\kappa(s_1)$, $\pi$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and $\pi^{-1}(\{y\})=\{w\}$, and $h$ is smooth of relative dimension $n$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] with geometrically integral fibres. Geometrically integral means that each fibre remains integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] after every extension of its residue field. Moreover $\kappa(y)/\kappa(s_1)$ is purely transcendental, meaning isomorphic over $\kappa(s_1)$ to a rational function field $\kappa(s_1)(t_1,\ldots,t_r)$ in algebraically independent variables for some $r\ge0$.

source.place: Tags 057K and 057L, lemma-local-local-structure-finite-type, clauses (1)--(6), and lemma-local-local-structure-finite-type-affine, clause (7).

proof.text: Choose an affine open $S^a\subset S$ containing $s$, and an affine open $Z^a\subset p^{-1}(S^a)$ containing $z$. The affine-pairs criterion makes $Z^a\to S^a$ finite type. The germ of the fibre at $z$ has not changed: by the open fibre-product identification, $(Z^a)_s=Z^a\times_{S^a}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is the open subscheme of $Z_s$ lying over $Z^a$, and open neighbourhoods inside an open neighbourhood form a cofinal system in the definition of topological dimension at a point. Thus its dimension is still $n$. Work with this affine pair; every later map to it will be composed with the open immersions into the original pair.

Apply the refined chart lemma to obtain $S_0,Z_0$ and $q:Z_0\to A=\mathbf A^n_{S_0}$, quasi-finite, with $t=q(z)$ and $\kappa(t)/\kappa(s)$ purely transcendental. The projection $A\to S_0$ is smooth of relative dimension $n$. Because the fibre of $q$ is finite discrete, $z$ is an isolated point in that fibre, so the hypotheses for the elementary etale finite-neighbourhood lemma hold for $q$ at $z$.

source.place: Tag 052E, refined polynomial chart before the elementary etale construction

proof.text: Apply the elementary etale finite-neighbourhood lemma to $q:Z_0\to A$. It gives $e:(Y_0,y_0)\to(A,t)$ etale with $\kappa(t)\simeq\kappa(y_0)$ and an open $W_0\subset Z_0\times_A Y_0$, finite over $Y_0$, whose fibre at $y_0$ is the single point $w_0$, mapping to $z$, with $\kappa(z)\simeq\kappa(w_0)$. The map $b_0:W_0\to Z$ is etale: it is an open immersion followed by the base change of $e$, then the open inclusion $Z_0\to Z$. The composite $h_0:Y_0\to A\to S_0$ is smooth of relative dimension $n$ by permanence, since $e$ has relative dimension zero. Its marked residue extension is purely transcendental.

source.place: Tag 052E, apply Tag 02LK over affine space, not over S

proof.text: Replace $Y_0$ by an affine open neighbourhood of $y_0$ and $W_0$ by its inverse image. Finiteness persists by base change, and this inverse image is open in the former $W_0$; hence the etale map to $Z$, the singleton fibre and marked residue fields persist. The restricted $h_0$ still has relative dimension $n$, since an open immersion is etale. Affine $Y_0$ and $S_0$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so $h_0$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Smoothness gives local finite presentation. Consequently $h_0$ is of finite presentation.

source.place: Tag 057K, affine neighbourhood of y and finite presentation of h

proof.text: The fibre $C=(Y_0)_s$ is smooth over $k=\kappa(s)$ by base change; it is finite type since it is affine and its structure map is locally of finite presentation. Its point $y_0$ has purely transcendental residue field over $k$. Apply the smooth component lemma: the connected component $T$ of $y_0$ is an open quasi-compact geometrically integral $k$-scheme. In particular it is geometrically irreducible, as required for the next step.

Apply elementary etale spreading to the finitely presented smooth $h_0:Y_0\to S_0$ and the geometrically irreducible open $T\subset (Y_0)_s$. It gives affine $(S_1,s_1)\to(S_0,s)$ etale with $\kappa(s_1)\simeq\kappa(s)$, and a quasi-compact open $V\subset Y_0\times_{S_0}S_1$ with geometrically integral fibres and $V_{s_1}=T\times_s s_1$. The map $V\to Y_0$ is etale, being the restriction of the base change of $S_1\to S_0$. The morphism $h_1:V\to S_1$ is smooth of relative dimension $n$ by base change and restriction to an open.

There is exactly one point $y_1$ of $Y_0\times_{S_0}S_1$ over the pair $(y_0,s_1)$: the fibre-product point correspondence identifies these points with primes of $\kappa(y_0)\otimes_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(s_1)\simeq\kappa(y_0)$, a field. Its residue field is $\kappa(y_0)$ compatibly with the projections, by the fibre-product residue-field theorem. Since $y_0\in T$ and $V_{s_1}=T\times_s s_1$, this point belongs to $V$. Therefore $\kappa(y_1)/\kappa(s_1)$ is the original purely transcendental extension under these field identifications.

source.place: Tag 057K, point (y,s′) and its residue field

proof.text: Set $W_1=W_0\times_{Y_0}V$, with projection $\pi_1:W_1\to V$. It is finite by base change. A point of its fibre at $y_1$ must map to $w_0$, since $w_0$ is the only point of $W_0$ over $y_0$. Points over $(w_0,y_1)$ correspond to primes of $\kappa(w_0)\otimes_{\kappa(y_0)}\kappa(y_1)\simeq\kappa(w_0)$. Thus there is exactly one such point $w_1$, and its residue field is $\kappa(w_0)$ compatibly with the projection; in particular $\kappa(z)\to\kappa(w_1)$ is an isomorphism. The map $W_1\to W_0$ is etale, as a base change of $V\to Y_0$, so $b_1:W_1\to Z$ is etale. The morphism $a_1:S_1\to S_0\to S$ is etale and elementary at $s_1$. The pullback identities give $pb_1=a_1h_1\pi_1$.

source.place: Tag 057K, final pullback and the omitted marked-point details

proof.text: For the affine refinement choose affine opens $U'\subset S_1$ around $s_1$ and $V'\subset h_1^{-1}(U')$ around $y_1$. Smoothness of $h_1$ implies flatness and local finite presentation, so $h_1$ is open. Hence $h_1(V')$ is an open neighbourhood of $s_1$ inside $U'$. Choose an affine open $U''\subset h_1(V')$ containing $s_1$, and set $Y=V'\cap h_1^{-1}(U'')$. The open fibre-product identification gives $Y=V'\times_{U'}U''$. All three schemes on the right are affine, so $Y$ is affine by the affine fibre-product formula. Put $S_1^{\mathrm{fin}}=U''$. By its choice, $Y\to U''$ is surjective; it is still smooth of relative dimension $n$, since the open immersion $Y\to V$ is etale and permanence applies with $m=0$.

Every fibre of $Y\to U''$ is a nonempty open subscheme of the corresponding geometrically integral fibre of $V\to S_1$. After any extension of the residue field it is still an open subscheme, by the open fibre-product formula, and remains nonempty by base-change stability of surjectivity. A nonempty open of an irreducible space is irreducible: two nonempty relatively open subsets are nonempty opens in the ambient space and must meet. Reducedness persists since its local rings are unchanged on passing to an open subscheme. Thus every extended fibre is nonempty, irreducible and reduced, hence integral by definition. This proves geometric integrality of the final fibres.

source.place: Tag 057L, nonempty opens in geometrically integral fibres

proof.text: Finally let $W=W_1\times_VY$ and restrict $\pi_1$ to $\pi:W\to Y$. This is finite, so $W$ is affine because $Y$ is affine. The points $y_1,w_1$ remain in these open subschemes; rename them $y,w$. The fibre at $y$ is still $\{w\}$. Open restrictions preserve all three marked residue fields, and the maps $b:W\to Z$ and $a:U''\to S$ remain etale by composition with open immersions. The relative dimension, geometric integrality and purely transcendental residue extension were retained in the preceding steps, while the commutative identity restricts to $pb=ah\pi$. Renaming $U''$ as $S_1$ gives every assertion of the item.
